title: Patch: a watched game's turn clock counts down, and a finished one stops saying Disconnected
thread:

```text
# #2974: Patch: a watched game's turn clock counts down, and a finished one stops saying Disconnected
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When you watch a friend's game, the turn clock shows a number that stays frozen while your friend thinks and jumps when they act, so you cannot tell how long they have left. And when the game ends normally, the status line says "Disconnected" beside the result, as if something broke. Once built, the clock ticks down between updates, silently, and a finished game says it is over.

## Why
- `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.tsx:329-344` passes the board no `turnClock`, so `game/Board.tsx:787` falls back to a static `formatSeconds(view.clockMs)`. The co-op watch's chrome (`WatchRoute.tsx:319`) has no clock either.
- The server fills `clockMs` into every watcher's frame (`crates/server/src/actor/match_actor.rs:828-839`, recorded by `spectate_record_in`, 2889-2897), so the number is there to count from. A player's own board ticks (`routes/match.tsx:513`, `game/Clock.tsx`).
- A finished game's socket closing sets the status to closed (`WatchRoute.tsx:185-187`), which reads "Disconnected" (lines 229-230), though the comment at line 270 already knows a finished game's socket closes as closed too.

## Proposal
- A small read-only countdown from each frame's `clockMs`, ticking from the frame's arrival, with no alarm, sound or haptic (the player's `Clock` plays the turn alarm, which a watcher must not hear). It is passed as `turnClock`, and to the co-op chrome.
- When the shown view has a result, the status line reads a finished game's words instead of the connection's.

## Where it lands
`apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.tsx`, possibly a small component in `apps/web/src/game/`, `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With fake timers, a frame with `clockMs` 60000 followed by 10 s shows 50; a new frame resets it.
- [ ] No sound or haptic cue plays from the watched clock.
- [ ] A finished frame followed by the socket's close shows no "Disconnected".
- [ ] The co-op watch shows the same ticking clock.

## Size and risks
Small. The countdown assumes the deadline holds between frames; a prompt or a timeout sends a new frame, which resets it. The board is `SPECTATE_DELAY_MS` behind and the clock is read at the same moment, so the two stay consistent.
```
